items.title: William Ballariel Interview, 1959-10-02
items.q: >> [SPEAKER_03] I noticed in a book, Mr. Malero, that it starts off again in 1939.

ctx.x: Well, they did that long time ago. Not when you were in the band. No, but one or two of them couldn't see good or something like that. Yes. They couldn't read, couldn't read, memorize the three. Many times playing those night parades and things, you didn't get sufficient lights to see the music. And you'd have to memorize the music. And some of them couldn't do it very well, and I was one that couldn't do it very well. Although, when I was playing alto, I had to draw lights, you see, but fairly connection to see…
I noticed in a book, Mr. Malero, that it starts off again in 1939. Did you leave the band for a while?

Yeah, I left the band for a while. I left the band for a while. They made me a band for some instance, and I quit for a while, but they insisted on me coming back and I went back, you see. I wondered too about in the... I stayed in it until I just got tired and went down, going down, so I just stayed in it. So practice going down and on. There's only three of us that played in the late year, a good while back. That's Johnny Pope, myself, and a fellow named Denny Trainor. I think his name's right, his name's…
